full_judgment:
32. In the case of Ramdayal Vs. Kailshi, A.I R. 1950 (Allahabad) 160 Malik, C.J. in a Division Bench case observes as follows :- 

 36. The next case relied upon by the learned Additional Attorney General is the case of Vasant Jaiwantrao Mahajan Vs. Tukaram Mohadaji Patil, AIR 1960 (Bom) 485 It has been held in this case that where a relevant provision of law this instance Order 9. rule 13 Proviso 1 as not been considered at the time of passing an order, such an order can be reviewed, if necessary, by the Judge who passes that order or by his successor But as already stated rule 2 of Order 47 has been omitted in 1950 in India. A judge who passes a decree or makes an order can himself or his successor may review the decree or order on the grounds stated in Order 47, rule 1 in India after the said amendment. This case therefore, is no authority for the proposition that the successor Judge can review the judgment of his predecessor Judge if there is an error of law apparent on the face of the judgment.
